messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize scope for the ServeFlow sprint: kernel selection heuristic, attention micro-ops, and KV eviction policy. Customer asks from AtlasPay and a few large B2B trials need clarity on launch gates.
ashwin: Can we separate "must-have" vs "nice-to-have"? I think KV eviction and basic kernel mux are musts. Attention micro-ops could be staged.
joel: Agreed. KV eviction impacts tail latency a lot for our customer workloads. If we can get a deterministic LRU-like policy with hook for model swap invalidation, that helps.
sophia: For attention ops: the optimization has two behaviors depending on seq_len. We need acceptance criteria that capture QoR regressions for short and long sequences separately.
tess: AtlasPay specifically called out long-chat contexts (8k+). They're seeing evictions that cause big latency spikes. They've asked for a guaranteed window for pinned prefixes.
maria: Proposal: priority 1 = KV eviction policy with prefix pinning + API to pin prefixes; priority 2 = kernel mux with lightweight heuristics for faster small-batch kernels; priority 3 = attention micro-ops rollout. Thoughts?
ashwin: Sounds good. For kernel mux, acceptance criteria: <5% p99 latency regression vs baseline on 99th percentile of tail workloads, and <3% token-cost increase.
joel: For KV: acceptance criteria: median eviction latency unaffected, p99 end-to-end latency improvement >=10% for high-eviction traces, and no correctness regressions (no stale KV reads). Also must support explicit API invalidation.
sophia: For attention ops: define QoR SLO as per-eval pass rate on our standard prompt suite; tolerate up to 0.5% regression on semantic metrics for short seq, 1% for long seq, but if regression >0.5% on either we block.
maria: Edge cases we must spec in RFC: model switch while KV in-flight, canary rollback on partial kernel failure, cross-tenant cache contamination prevention, and quantized kernel numeric edgecases.
tess: Can we expose a config flag to control prefix pin TTL and also a hard pin API? AtlasPay wants hard pins. Security-wise it's fine?
ashwin: Hard pin API is ok, but requires validation in the control plane and quota accounting. Add a per-tenant pinned-kv limit.
joel: Operational launch gates: staging perf tests green for 48h, canary at 5% traffic for 24h with synthetic load + production shadow for an additional 24h, full rollout if error increase <0.05% and latency within thresholds.
sophia: Add automated quality checks on the eval harness each merge: run short & long evals, do monotonic regression checks. Fail CI if QoR drops beyond threshold.
maria: Can someone draft the PRD+RFC checklist items? I want: brief motivation, success metrics, acceptance tests, canary plan, rollback strategy, perf matrix, security considerations, API contract for pin/invalidate.
ashwin: I'll take the PRD draft and add kernel mux perf matrix. ETA EOD tomorrow.
ess: sorry typo — tess meant: I'll coordinate AtlasPay validation tests.
tess: I'll own customer validation and the pinned-prefix API contract with their PM.
joel: I'll write the KV eviction design doc and the canary orchestration runbook. Will include the k8s job for warmup + the monitor alerts to block rollout.
sophia: I'll add the eval harness configs and regression dashboards.
maria: Risk register quick notes: 1) numeric divergence in quantized kernels -> mitigation: fallback to fp kernel per-tenant; 2) cache pollution -> mitigation: per-tenant namespace + hard pins; 3) canary flaps -> automation to revert and throttle.
ashwin: For the fp fallback: we need a perf guard so fallback doesn't blow up costs. Set threshold: if fallback increases latency by >2x on p95, abort rollout.
joel: Monitoring: add these signals — token latency p50/p95/p99, evictions/sec, cache hit ratio, model-switch errors, kernel-fallback rate, QoR regression alert.
maria: Meeting? Let's do RFC review Thurs 10am. Put initial PRD link in thread when ready.
tess: @maria noted. I'll invite AtlasPay PM for the RFC review to confirm acceptance criteria.
ashwin: Quick question on edge-case: what happens if a model roll includes a new KV key format? We need migration strategy in RFC.
joel: Migration strategy options: rolling-incompatible update (drain + flush) or compatibility shim in runtime that understands old/new formats. Recommend shim for low-risk, drain for high-risk. Add cost estimation for both.
sophia: Also test for sequence trimming interactions with pinned prefixes. Long sequences + pin should not cause prefix chop. Add test vectors.
maria: Assignments recap: Nashwin PRD + kernel perf matrix; Joel KV design + runbook; Sophia evals + dashboards; Tess customer validation + API contract. I'll consolidate into RFC doc.
ashwin: One more: can we gate attention micro-ops behind a feature flag per-tenant? Helps rollback.
ess: again typo — joel? (meant: yes)
joel: Yes, feature flag + kernel-level capability check.
maria: Great. If everyone is OK, I'll mark scope and generate the RFC template by EOD.
ashwin: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary scheduled — 5% traffic next Tuesday 03:00 UTC for KV-eviction-v1 on staging. Logs: <link://canary/2476543210>\"
